text: Coverage: two East African primary health care operations read in detail; other PHC projects (for example in Nigeria, Ethiopia or Uganda) use similar indicators.

1. Kenya - Transforming Health Systems for Universal Care (P152394), PAD 2016 (pp. 46-49). PDO: improve utilization and quality of primary health care services with a focus on RMNCAH. PDO indicators, baseline to end target: children under 1 fully immunized 73% to 76%; pregnant women with at least four ANC visits 40% to 46%; births attended by skilled personnel 57% to 64%; women 15-49 using modern family planning 41% to 45%; inspected facilities meeting safety standards 0% to 50%. Intermediate indicators include functional community units 1,549 to 2,400; ANC attendees given iron-folic acid 31% to 40%; facilities providing basic emergency obstetric care 39% to 60%; facilities submitting complete, timely DHIS data 76% to 85%; birth registration 60% to 80%; people receiving essential health, nutrition and population services 3,704,547 to 4,200,000. Data sources: DHIS2 (collected by county departments of health) for the service-coverage indicators; administrative inspection data using the Joint Health Inspection Checklist (MoH Quality Standards) for safety standards; Master Community Unit listing; Master Facility List for BEmOC; civil registration annual report for births; grievance registers and project status reports for process indicators (pp. 48-49).

2. Tanzania - Strengthening Primary Health Care for Results (P152736), PforR, ICR 2022 (pp. 14, 39-41). PDO: improve the quality of PHC services nationwide with a focus on MNCH. PDO indicators with baseline (Aug 2015), original target, revised target and result: PHC facilities rated 3 stars or above 0%, 50%, revised 30%, achieved 19% (2018; the third assessment round was not carried out); pregnant women with four or more ANC visits 41.2%, 60%, 68%, 90%; ANC attendees receiving two doses of malaria IPT 42.52%, 60%, 80%, 79%; institutional deliveries 44.72%, 60%, 70%, 83%; children 12-59 months receiving vitamin A 51%, 65%, 90%, 100%. Intermediate indicators include health's share of the government budget (8.5% baseline, target 9.75%, result 7%) and completeness of quarterly HMIS data in DHIS (89.5% baseline, target 95%, result 96%) (pp. 18, 41). Data sources: the national Star Rating assessment of all PHC facilities for the quality indicator (p. 23, fn. 8 p. 14) and the routine HMIS/DHIS2 for service indicators (pp. 18, 21).

Common choices: ANC4+, skilled or institutional delivery and immunization as coverage measures from routine DHIS2 data; a facility quality score from a national assessment tool (Star Rating, JHIC); data-quality indicators (DHIS completeness) because the routine system is the main source.
